//: Type-checking, scoped by evidence rather than ambition.
Running tsc --checkJs over all of js/ reports 225 errors, and they were
counted before this file was written rather than assumed: roughly 90 are
DOM narrowing (getElementById returns HTMLElement, so .value and .disabled
and .dataset all complain), 17 are the untyped `three` import, and a dozen
more are TS inference limits on [RegExp, string] tuple arrays. None of
them is a bug. Clearing them means casts at ~90 call sites or a typed-DOM
helper refactor across every screen — a lot of edits to files that are not
The data layer is 21 errors and is where the bugs actually lived: answers
bleeding between saved spaces, a serializer that drifted from its reader,
an analysis writing over newer state. Those files are checked here, so the
AppState typedef in state.js is enforced rather than aspirational.
Adding a screen file to `include` is welcome — expect DOM casts with it.
